verdict: McCormick's sales jumped 17% after it bought control of its Mexican joint venture, but deal costs and a $43M write-off cut GAAP profit 57% to $98M — underlying EPS was steady at $0.86.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Spices, herbs and recipe mixes sold in grocery stores (McCormick, Frank's RedHot, French's). Growth was mostly the McCormick de Mexico acquisition; organic sales rose 1%.

segments.name: Flavor Solutions
segments.note: Flavorings sold to food and drink manufacturers and restaurants — organic sales rose 3%.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Brand marketing, the sales force and back office — higher this year with the Mexico business consolidated and more brand investment.

opex.name: Special charges
opex.note: Costs of the planned Unilever Foods combination and integration work, plus a $43M non-cash impairment and exit costs from closing a pepper-sourcing project in Malaysia.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $68M, partly offset by $6M of other income, net.
oneTimers: $141.5M of special charges — transaction and integration costs for the planned combination with Unilever Foods plus a $43.1M non-cash impairment and $1.8M of exit costs on a development-stage pepper project in Malaysia — cut EPS by $0.50. Excluding special charges, adjusted operating income rose 22% to $359M and adjusted EPS was $0.86.

takeaways.title: An acquisition did the growing
takeaways.text: Buying the rest of McCormick de Mexico (closed January 2026) contributed about 15 points of the 17% sales growth. Organic growth was 2%, driven by price.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded anyway
takeaways.text: Gross margin widened 190 basis points to 39.3% on the Mexico contribution, cost savings from the CCI program, and pricing — absorbing higher commodity and freight costs.

takeaways.title: Deal costs dominate the GAAP line
takeaways.text: Special charges of $141.5M — mostly for the planned Unilever Foods combination — took $0.50 off EPS. Adjusted EPS of $0.86 was up just 1%, as higher interest and tax offset 22% adjusted operating income growth.

footerNote: This is McCormick's fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended August 31, 2026). Figures are rounded to whole $M from the release's one-decimal presentation, with $1M of rounding absorbed in Consumer segment sales. The small 'equity' line nets $3M of income from unconsolidated operations against $10M of profit attributable to noncontrolling interests (mainly Grupo Herdez's 25% of McCormick de Mexico). A transformational combination with Unilever Foods was announced in March 2026 and is expected to close by mid-2027.
